propositions.text: Applicant seeks judicial review of two CRA decisions communicated by a Second Level Reviewer.
Reviewer found Mr. Li ineligible for CERB and CRB benefits.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant seeks judicial review of CRA decisions denying CERB and CRB eligibility, found by Second Level Reviewer.

propositions.text: Application for judicial review will be granted in part.

paragraphs.summary: Court grants the application for judicial review in part.

propositions.text: Mr. Li worked full-time in a warehouse and quit in July 2020 for childcare and COVID-19 concerns.
He then took flexible part-time delivery work including Instacart.

paragraphs.summary: Mr. Li quit warehouse job in July 2020 for childcare and COVID-19 concerns and took part-time delivery work.

propositions.text: Mr. Li applied for and received CERB from Aug 30 to Sept 26, 2020, and CRB from Oct 11, 2020 to July 17, 2021.

paragraphs.summary: Mr. Li received CERB and CRB benefits for specified periods due to income reduction from COVID-19.

propositions.text: CRA contacted Mr. Li on July 2, 2024, to confirm eligibility for CERB and CRB.

paragraphs.summary: CRA requested confirmation of Mr. Li's CERB and CRB eligibility in July 2024.

propositions.text: Mr. Li provided supporting documents including a letter about job loss due to COVID-19 lockdown and Instacart earnings.

paragraphs.summary: Mr. Li submitted documents including a letter and Instacart earnings to CRA.

propositions.text: First Level Reviewer called Mr. Li on Sept 25, 2024, requesting more documents.
Mr. Li stated he was laid off as non-essential, willing to work, and EI was not an option.
Reviewer requested ROEs, invoices, and expense reports; Mr. Li lacked these documents.

paragraphs.summary: First Level Reviewer requested documents; Mr. Li said he was laid off, willing to work, but lacked requested documents.

propositions.text: On Oct 1, 2024, Reviewer clarified documents needed to show Instacart income.

paragraphs.summary: Reviewer clarified required documents to Mr. Li for Instacart income proof.

propositions.text: First Level Reviewer found Mr. Li ineligible for CERB due to earning over $1,000 and not stopping work for COVID-19 reasons.
Found ineligible for CRB due to no 50% income reduction and lack of documents.

paragraphs.summary: First Level Reviewer found Mr. Li ineligible for CERB and CRB due to income and lack of documents.

propositions.text: Mr. Li requested a second review of his eligibility.

paragraphs.summary: Mr. Li requested a second level review of eligibility.

propositions.text: Second Level Reviewer called Mr. Li on July 29, 2025; Mr. Li attested quitting due to COVID-19 fear and childcare needs.

paragraphs.summary: Second Level Reviewer recorded Mr. Li's statement about quitting due to COVID-19 fear and childcare.

propositions.text: Reviewer found Mr. Li ineligible for CERB and CRB because he quit voluntarily, not for COVID-19 reasons, per relevant Acts.
Reviewer did not assess income documentation due to voluntary quit finding.

paragraphs.summary: Reviewer denied benefits based on voluntary quit and did not assess income documents.

propositions.text: Second Level Review decision issued July 31, 2025, stating ineligibility due to voluntary quitting and no COVID-19 related work stoppage.

paragraphs.summary: Second Level Review decision stated ineligibility due to voluntary quitting and no COVID-19 related work stoppage.

propositions.text: Letter also stated ineligibility for CERB due to earning over $1,000 and CRB due to no 50% income reduction.

paragraphs.summary: Letter noted ineligibility for CERB and CRB due to income thresholds and reductions.

propositions.text: Mr. Li disagrees with Second Level Review decision and argues it should be overturned and process was unfair.
Standard of review for CRA decisions on CERB and CRB is reasonableness, per cited cases.

paragraphs.summary: Mr. Li challenges decision and process fairness; court states reasonableness standard applies.

propositions.text: Court reviews procedural fairness by its own analysis, applying correctness standard.
Procedural fairness owed to CERB and CRB applicants is low.

paragraphs.summary: Court applies correctness standard to procedural fairness, which is low for CERB and CRB applicants.

propositions.text: CRA decision based on findings: CERB - earned over $1,000, quit voluntarily, no COVID-19 related work stoppage; CRB - quit voluntarily, no 50% income reduction due to COVID-19.

paragraphs.summary: CRA decision findings on CERB and CRB eligibility summarized.

propositions.text: Respondent concedes CERB income finding and CRB income reduction finding were errors due to no income calculations.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent concedes errors in income-related findings for CERB and CRB.

propositions.text: Court questioned Respondent about CRB Act s 3(1)(k) regarding quitting before Sept 27, 2020.
Respondent conceded relying on Mr. Li's resignation before Sept 27, 2020, to deny CRB was unreasonable.

paragraphs.summary: Court questioned Respondent on CRB quitting date; Respondent conceded unreasonableness.

propositions.text: Respondent amends argument, submits Court should grant application regarding CRB findings due to conceded errors.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent submits Court should grant application on CRB findings due to conceded errors.

propositions.text: Application for judicial review granted regarding CRB findings as they are unjustified under CRB Act paragraph 3(1)(k).

paragraphs.summary: The court grants judicial review for CRB findings as unjustified under CRB Act paragraph 3(1)(k).

propositions.text: Reviewer’s conclusion that Applicant voluntarily quit job and was ineligible for CERB was reasonable and fair.
Agrees that the CERB decision was reasonable and fair.

paragraphs.summary: The respondent argues the CERB decision was reasonable and fair; the court agrees.

propositions.text: Paragraph 6(1)(a) of CERB Act defines eligibility for income support payment related to COVID-19 work cessation.

paragraphs.summary: Paragraph 6(1)(a) of CERB Act defines eligibility for income support related to COVID-19 work cessation.

propositions.text: Subsection 6(2) of CERB Act excludes voluntary quitting from 'ceases work' definition for eligibility.

paragraphs.summary: Subsection 6(2) of CERB Act excludes voluntary quitting from 'ceases work' for eligibility.

propositions.text: Applicant ceased work by voluntarily quitting; he was not terminated or laid off.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Applicant voluntarily quit work and was not terminated or laid off.

propositions.text: Applicant was not forthcoming with CRA about reason for stopping work, initially claiming layoff.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Applicant misrepresented to CRA that he was laid off, not quit.

propositions.text: Applicant communicated through interpreter but conveyed inaccurate information to CRA about job cessation.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Applicant conveyed inaccurate job cessation information to CRA despite interpreter use.

propositions.text: It was reasonable for Second Level Reviewer to conclude Applicant voluntarily quit despite Applicant's claim of non-voluntariness due to COVID-19 fears and childcare.
Cites Bui v Canada and Phipps v Canada supporting reasonableness of voluntary quit conclusion.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the voluntary quit conclusion reasonable, citing Bui and Phipps cases.

propositions.text: Applicant argues process was unfair due to lack of findings on resignation in First Review and surprise at Second Review decision.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues process was unfair due to surprise and lack of findings on resignation in First Review.

propositions.text: Applicant had adequate notice and fair opportunity despite some sympathy for his argument.
Applicant's misrepresentations to CRA do not support unfair treatment claim.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Applicant had adequate notice and misrepresentations do not support unfair treatment claim.

propositions.text: Judicial review dismissed for CERB decision; granted for CRB decision with remand to CRA for redetermination.
No costs awarded due to Applicant's mixed success.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses CERB review, grants CRB review with remand, and awards no costs due to mixed success.
